questions.q: Which shortcut **centres** the selected paragraph in Word?
questions.solution: **Ctrl+E = cEntre.** Ctrl+C is copy; C was taken, so centre borrowed E.

questions.q: The Wi-Fi wireless LAN standard family is designated by IEEE:
questions.solution: IEEE 802.11 covers Wi-Fi (a/b/g/n/ac/ax). 802.3 is wired Ethernet, 802.15 Bluetooth/PAN, 802.16 WiMAX.

questions.q: Which statement is correct?
options: Ctrl+H shows history but Ctrl+H in Word opens Replace
Ctrl+H shows history in every program
Ctrl+D bookmarks a page and duplicates slides in Word
Alt+Home opens the browser's download page
questions.solution: Ctrl+H is **History in browsers, Replace in Word** — same keys, different apps. Ctrl+D duplicates slides in PowerPoint, not Word; the browser home page is Alt+Home (that part of option D is right but its download-page tail is wrong).
questions.shortcut: Same key, three apps, three jobs.

questions.q: A Class C network provides how many USABLE host addresses?
questions.solution: 256 total minus the **network address** and the **broadcast address** = **254 usable**.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She is not capable ___ handling so much pressure at work.
questions.solution: The fixed collocation is **capable of** + V-ing. *capable for / in / to* are not standard.

questions.q:
Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.

VIGILANT
questions.solution: *Vigilant* = carefully watchful for danger → **alert**. 'Careless' and 'drowsy' are opposite-directed; 'hostile' shifts to temperament.

questions.q: Select the word which is most opposite in meaning to the given word.  VICTORIOUS
questions.solution: Command word = opposite. Strike the synonym decoys (triumphant, winning, successful) → **defeated**.

questions.q: Select the word which is nearest in meaning to the given word.  CHRONOLOGICAL
questions.solution: chron = time → **arranged in time order** (a chronology of events).

questions.q: Dengue fever is transmitted by which mosquito?
questions.solution: **Dengue** (a viral disease) is spread by the day-biting **Aedes** mosquito (*Aedes aegypti*), which also spreads chikungunya, Zika and yellow fever. Anopheles spreads malaria and Culex spreads filariasis.

questions.q: The RBI's single, integrated scheme for resolving customer complaints against banks and other regulated entities was introduced in:
questions.solution: The **RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, 2021** merged the old Banking Ombudsman Scheme (1995) and other schemes into one cost-free complaint route through the RBI's central portal.

questions.q: **Gond** tribal painting is associated with —
questions.solution: **Gond** painting — the dot-and-line tribal art of the Gond community of central India (MP).

questions.q: Digboi, the site of India's oldest oil refinery, is located in which state?
questions.solution: The **Digboi** refinery in **Assam** began operating in **1901** and is the oldest operating refinery in India. Gujarat has Ankleshwar and Koyali; Mumbai High is an offshore field off Maharashtra.

questions.q: A 240 m long train running at 90 km/h crosses a cyclist coming from the opposite direction at 18 km/h. The train crosses him in:
A and B invest ₹45,000 and ₹35,000 in a business for one year. Out of a profit of ₹8,000, A's share is:
The minimum value of $\tan^2\theta + \cot^2\theta$ ($\theta$ acute) is:
questions.solution: With $x = \tan^2\theta$: $x + \frac1x \ge 2$, equality at $x = 1$ i.e. $\theta = 45^\circ$.
questions.shortcut: $2$ at $45^\circ$. Trap: $0$ — a positive term and its reciprocal cannot both vanish.

questions.q: An article marked at ₹1,600 is sold for ₹1,224 after two successive discounts. If the first discount is 15%, the second discount is:
questions.shortcut: 12% would be (1360 − 1224)/... on the MP — the second discount is on ₹1,360.

questions.q:
Three of the following four pairs are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd pair.

**Hot : Cold, Up : Down, Rich : Poor, Big : Large**
questions.solution: Hot - cold, up - down and rich - poor are **opposites**. Big and large have the **same meaning** → **Big : Large**.

questions.q: If **a ▲ b = a − b** when a > b and **a ▲ b = a + b** when a ≤ b, find **(9 ▲ 4) ▲ 7**.
questions.solution: 9 ▲ 4: 9 > 4, so 9 − 4 = 5. Then 5 ▲ 7: 5 ≤ 7, so 5 + 7 = **12**. (−2 re-uses the first case without checking.)
questions.shortcut: Check the condition again at every step.

questions.q: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.solution: The inner square joins the midpoints; the diagonals of the outer square cross everything. Size by size: each corner triangle is split by a diagonal into 2 tiny ones → 8; the 4 corner triangles themselves → 4; the 4 triangles with a full side of the square as base and apex at the centre → 4; the 4 half-squares → 4. Total 8 + 4 + 4 + 4 = **20**.
questions.shortcut: Work outward: tiny, corner, centre-apex, half-square.

questions.q:
Three of the following four number-sets are alike in a certain way and one is different. Find the odd set.
(**NOTE:** Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking them into their digits. For example, with 13 you may add, subtract or multiply 13 itself, but you may not split it into 1 and 3.)

**(7, 3, 20), (8, 5, 39), (6, 4, 23), (9, 2, 18)**
questions.shortcut: Third number is one less than the product in three sets, equal to it in one.
